market_question: Will the US acquire part of Greenland in 2026?
reasoning: Given firm opposition from Denmark and Greenland, no ongoing negotiations, and the implausibility of a forced acquisition, the true probability of a binding agreement transferring sovereignty or exclusive jurisdiction over any Greenland territory by end of 2026 is very low, around 6%. The market price of 13.5% significantly overstates this chance.
evidence_points: Greenland and Danish officials have consistently declared Greenland is not for sale and rejected US acquisition overtures.
No formal legislation, treaty, or executive action is in progress to transfer any part of Greenland to US control.
Existing US military presence (Pituffik Space Base) operates under Danish sovereignty with no exclusive US jurisdiction.
Use of force to acquire territory is extremely unlikely and would violate international norms.
sources_consulted: Reuters reports on Trump's Greenland interest and Denmark's rejection
